newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says it, EU extend steel agreement 6 mths.
newsitem.headline: Russia says it, EU extend steel agreement 6 mths.

text.p: Russia and the European Union have extended a steel export agreement set to expire at the end of December for six months while negotiators hammer out a new accord, a Russian foreign trade official said on Monday.

"Since we were late starting the negotiations, we decided to prolong the duration of the present agreement for the time of the negotiations," said Alexei Litvyakov, head of the Foreign Economic Relations Ministry's European Union unit.
Litvyakov said Russia would seek in the new accord to increase access to European markets, which limit Russian steel imports by category of steel product under the present agreement.

"The extension is for six months or until the new agreement comes into force," he said by telephone, adding that Russian and European representatives had initialed the extension in November and would formalise the extension later this month.
He said formal negotiations, which have not begun yet, would start in January, probably in Brussels.
"There will be some sort of agreement on competition rules in order to put our industry and the EC industry in the same competitive environment," he said.
"There will be some rules on competition and practices -- no (state) subsidising, for example, or some discipline in state aid," he added.
European Trade Commissioner Leon Brittan met Russian Foreign Economic Relations Minister Oleg Davydov on November 21 and called for Russia to liberalise its steel industry.
